{"schema_version":1,"rules":[
{"id":"harden.ssh.permit_root_login","version":1,"title":"SSH allows root to log in with a password","severity":"high","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sshd.permitrootlogin'] == 'yes' || facts['sshd.permitrootlogin'] == 'Yes' || facts['sshd.permitrootlogin'] == 'YES'","finding_message":"sshd lets root log in with a password (PermitRootLogin yes). Set it to prohibit-password or no, and log in as a named user.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0001","technique":"T1078.003"},{"tactic":"TA0008","technique":"T1021.004"}]},
{"id":"harden.ssh.password_authentication","version":1,"title":"SSH accepts passwords","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sshd.passwordauthentication'] != 'no' && facts['sshd.passwordauthentication'] != 'No' && facts['sshd.passwordauthentication'] != 'NO'","finding_message":"sshd accepts password logins (PasswordAuthentication is yes or not set), which password guessing can reach. Use keys and set PasswordAuthentication no.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1110"}]},
{"id":"harden.ssh.permit_empty_passwords","version":1,"title":"SSH allows empty passwords","severity":"high","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sshd.permitemptypasswords'] == 'yes' || facts['sshd.permitemptypasswords'] == 'Yes' || facts['sshd.permitemptypasswords'] == 'YES'","finding_message":"sshd lets accounts with an empty password log in (PermitEmptyPasswords yes). Set it to no.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0001","technique":"T1078.003"}]},
{"id":"harden.ssh.hostbased_authentication","version":1,"title":"SSH trusts other hosts","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sshd.hostbasedauthentication'] == 'yes' || facts['sshd.hostbasedauthentication'] == 'Yes' || facts['sshd.hostbasedauthentication'] == 'YES'","finding_message":"sshd accepts host-based authentication (HostbasedAuthentication yes): a user trusted on another host logs in here without a password. Set it to no.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0008","technique":"T1021.004"}]},
{"id":"harden.ssh.ignore_rhosts","version":1,"title":"SSH reads .rhosts files","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sshd.ignorerhosts'] == 'no' || facts['sshd.ignorerhosts'] == 'No' || facts['sshd.ignorerhosts'] == 'NO'","finding_message":"sshd honours users' .rhosts and .shosts files (IgnoreRhosts no). Set it to yes.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0008","technique":"T1021.004"}]},
{"id":"harden.ssh.permit_user_environment","version":1,"title":"SSH lets users set the login environment","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sshd.permituserenvironment'] == 'yes' || facts['sshd.permituserenvironment'] == 'Yes' || facts['sshd.permituserenvironment'] == 'YES'","finding_message":"sshd reads users' ~/.ssh/environment (PermitUserEnvironment yes), which can bypass restrictions such as LD_PRELOAD rules. Set it to no.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0004","technique":"T1548"}]},
{"id":"harden.ssh.max_auth_tries","version":1,"title":"SSH allows many login attempts per connection","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sshd.maxauthtries'] > 4 || facts['sshd.maxauthtries'] == -1","finding_message":"sshd allows more than 4 authentication attempts per connection (MaxAuthTries, default 6). Set MaxAuthTries 4 or lower.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1110"}]},
{"id":"harden.ssh.login_grace_time","version":1,"title":"SSH waits long for a login","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sshd.logingracetime'] > 60 || facts['sshd.logingracetime'] == -1 || facts['sshd.logingracetime'] == 0","finding_message":"sshd keeps unauthenticated connections open for more than 60 seconds (LoginGraceTime, default 120; 0 is no limit). Set LoginGraceTime 60 or lower.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1110"}]},
{"id":"harden.ssh.x11_forwarding","version":1,"title":"SSH forwards X11","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sshd.x11forwarding'] == 'yes' || facts['sshd.x11forwarding'] == 'Yes' || facts['sshd.x11forwarding'] == 'YES'","finding_message":"sshd forwards X11 (X11Forwarding yes), which exposes the client's display to the server. Set it to no unless people run graphical programs over SSH.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0008","technique":"T1021.004"}]},
{"id":"harden.ssh.log_level","version":1,"title":"SSH logs too little","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sshd.loglevel'] == 'quiet' || facts['sshd.loglevel'] == 'Quiet' || facts['sshd.loglevel'] == 'QUIET' || facts['sshd.loglevel'] == 'fatal' || facts['sshd.loglevel'] == 'Fatal' || facts['sshd.loglevel'] == 'FATAL' || facts['sshd.loglevel'] == 'error' || facts['sshd.loglevel'] == 'Error' || facts['sshd.loglevel'] == 'ERROR'","finding_message":"sshd logs too little to see logins (LogLevel QUIET, FATAL or ERROR). Set LogLevel INFO or VERBOSE.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0112","technique":"T1685"}]},
{"id":"harden.ssh.config_permissions","version":1,"title":"sshd_config is open to other users","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"(facts['file.etc_sshd_config.mode'] != '' && facts['file.etc_sshd_config.mode'] != '0600' && facts['file.etc_sshd_config.mode'] != '0640' && facts['file.etc_sshd_config.mode'] != '0400' && facts['file.etc_sshd_config.mode'] != '0440' && !(facts['file.etc_sshd_config.mode'] == '0644' && ('debian' in facts['os.id_like'] || 'ubuntu' in facts['os.id_like'] || 'arch' in facts['os.id_like']))) || (facts['file.etc_sshd_config.owner'] != '' && !facts['file.etc_sshd_config.owner'].startsWith('0:'))","finding_message":"/etc/ssh/sshd_config can be read or changed by users other than root (accepted: 0600, 0640 or stricter; also 0644, the stock mode on Debian, Ubuntu and Arch), or is not owned by root. Make it root:root 0600.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1003"}]},
{"id":"harden.kernel.aslr","version":1,"title":"Address space randomisation is weakened","severity":"high","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.kernel.randomize_va_space'] != 2","finding_message":"kernel.randomize_va_space is not 2, so memory layouts are easier to predict for an exploit. Set it to 2.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0004","technique":"T1068"}]},
{"id":"harden.kernel.ptrace_scope","version":1,"title":"Any process can trace another of the same user","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.kernel.yama.ptrace_scope'] == 0","finding_message":"kernel.yama.ptrace_scope is 0: any process can attach to another process of the same user and read its memory. Set it to 1.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0004","technique":"T1055.008"}]},
{"id":"harden.kernel.unprivileged_bpf","version":1,"title":"Unprivileged users can load BPF programs","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled'] == 0","finding_message":"kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled is 0: any user can load BPF programs, a frequent kernel exploit path. Set it to 1 or 2.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0004","technique":"T1068"}]},
{"id":"harden.kernel.kptr_restrict","version":1,"title":"Kernel addresses are visible to users","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.kernel.kptr_restrict'] == 0","finding_message":"kernel.kptr_restrict is 0: kernel pointers are shown to users, which helps kernel exploits. Set it to 1.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0004","technique":"T1068"}]},
{"id":"harden.kernel.dmesg_restrict","version":1,"title":"Users can read the kernel log","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.kernel.dmesg_restrict'] == 0","finding_message":"kernel.dmesg_restrict is 0: any user can read the kernel log, including addresses and hardware details. Set it to 1.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0007","technique":"T1082"}]},
{"id":"harden.fs.protected_links","version":1,"title":"Link protections are off","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.fs.protected_hardlinks'] == 0 || facts['sysctl.fs.protected_symlinks'] == 0","finding_message":"fs.protected_hardlinks or fs.protected_symlinks is 0, which allows link tricks in shared directories such as /tmp. Set both to 1.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0004","technique":"T1068"}]},
{"id":"harden.fs.suid_dumpable","version":1,"title":"Privileged programs can write core dumps","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.fs.suid_dumpable'] != 0 && !facts['sysctl.kernel.core_pattern_pipe']","finding_message":"fs.suid_dumpable is not 0 and cores are written to files, so a crashing privileged program can leave its memory, secrets included, on disk. Set it to 0, or send cores to a handler such as systemd-coredump.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1003"}]},
{"id":"harden.net.ip_forward","version":1,"title":"The host forwards IP packets","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.net.ipv4.ip_forward'] == 1 && !('docker' in facts['package.names'] || 'docker-ce' in facts['package.names'] || 'moby-engine' in facts['package.names'] || 'podman' in facts['package.names'] || 'containerd' in facts['package.names'] || 'containerd.io' in facts['package.names'] || 'cri-o' in facts['package.names'] || 'kubelet' in facts['package.names'] || 'docker.service' in facts['service.active'] || 'podman.service' in facts['service.active'] || 'containerd.service' in facts['service.active'] || 'crio.service' in facts['service.active'] || 'kubelet.service' in facts['service.active'])","finding_message":"net.ipv4.ip_forward is 1 on a host with no container runtime, so it routes packets between networks. Set it to 0 unless this host is a router.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0112","technique":"T1599"}]},
{"id":"harden.net.send_redirects","version":1,"title":"The host sends ICMP redirects","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"(facts['sysctl.net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects'] == 1 || facts['sysctl.net.ipv4.conf.default.send_redirects'] == 1) && facts['sysctl.net.ipv4.ip_forward'] == 0","finding_message":"The host is not a router but sends ICMP redirects (net.ipv4.conf.all or default send_redirects is 1), which can steer other hosts' traffic. Set both to 0.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1557"}]},
{"id":"harden.net.accept_source_route","version":1,"title":"The host accepts source-routed IPv4 packets","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route'] == 1","finding_message":"net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route is 1: the sender chooses the route, which can bypass filtering. Set it to 0.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1557"}]},
{"id":"harden.net.accept_source_route_v6","version":1,"title":"The host accepts source-routed IPv6 packets","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_source_route'] == 1","finding_message":"net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_source_route is 1: the sender chooses the route, which can bypass filtering. Set it to 0.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1557"}]},
{"id":"harden.net.accept_redirects","version":1,"title":"The host accepts IPv4 ICMP redirects","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects'] == 1","finding_message":"net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects is 1: another host can change this host's routes. Set it to 0.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1557"}]},
{"id":"harden.net.accept_redirects_v6","version":1,"title":"The host accepts IPv6 ICMP redirects","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_redirects'] == 1","finding_message":"net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_redirects is 1: another host can change this host's routes. Set it to 0.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1557"}]},
{"id":"harden.net.icmp_broadcasts","version":1,"title":"The host answers broadcast pings","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.net.ipv4.icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts'] == 0","finding_message":"net.ipv4.icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts is 0: the host answers pings to broadcast addresses, which amplifies floods. Set it to 1.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0040","technique":"T1499"}]},
{"id":"harden.net.syncookies","version":1,"title":"SYN cookies are off","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies'] == 0","finding_message":"net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies is 0, so a SYN flood can fill the connection queue. Set it to 1.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0040","technique":"T1499"}]},
{"id":"harden.net.rp_filter","version":1,"title":"Reverse path filtering is off","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['sysctl.net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter'] == 0","finding_message":"net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter is 0: packets with spoofed source addresses are accepted. Set it to 1 (strict) or 2 (loose).","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1557"}]},
{"id":"harden.files.shadow","version":1,"title":"/etc/shadow is open to other users","severity":"high","confidence":90,"expression":"(facts['file.etc_shadow.mode'] != '' && !facts['file.etc_shadow.mode'].endsWith('0')) || (facts['file.etc_shadow.owner'] != '' && !facts['file.etc_shadow.owner'].startsWith('0:')) || (facts['file.etc_shadow_backup.mode'] != '' && !facts['file.etc_shadow_backup.mode'].endsWith('0')) || (facts['file.etc_shadow_backup.owner'] != '' && !facts['file.etc_shadow_backup.owner'].startsWith('0:'))","finding_message":"/etc/shadow (or its backup /etc/shadow-) can be read by other users or is not owned by root; it holds the password hashes. Make it owned by root with no access for others (0640 or 0000).","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1003.008"}]},
{"id":"harden.files.gshadow","version":1,"title":"/etc/gshadow is open to other users","severity":"high","confidence":90,"expression":"(facts['file.etc_gshadow.mode'] != '' && !facts['file.etc_gshadow.mode'].endsWith('0')) || (facts['file.etc_gshadow.owner'] != '' && !facts['file.etc_gshadow.owner'].startsWith('0:')) || (facts['file.etc_gshadow_backup.mode'] != '' && !facts['file.etc_gshadow_backup.mode'].endsWith('0')) || (facts['file.etc_gshadow_backup.owner'] != '' && !facts['file.etc_gshadow_backup.owner'].startsWith('0:'))","finding_message":"/etc/gshadow (or its backup /etc/gshadow-) can be read by other users or is not owned by root; it holds group password hashes. Make it owned by root with no access for others.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1003.008"}]},
{"id":"harden.files.passwd","version":1,"title":"/etc/passwd or /etc/group can be changed by other users","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"(facts['file.etc_passwd.mode'] != '' && facts['file.etc_passwd.mode'] != '0644' && facts['file.etc_passwd.mode'] != '0640' && facts['file.etc_passwd.mode'] != '0600' && facts['file.etc_passwd.mode'] != '0444' && facts['file.etc_passwd.mode'] != '0440' && facts['file.etc_passwd.mode'] != '0400') || (facts['file.etc_group.mode'] != '' && facts['file.etc_group.mode'] != '0644' && facts['file.etc_group.mode'] != '0640' && facts['file.etc_group.mode'] != '0600' && facts['file.etc_group.mode'] != '0444' && facts['file.etc_group.mode'] != '0440' && facts['file.etc_group.mode'] != '0400')","finding_message":"/etc/passwd or /etc/group has a mode other than 0644 or stricter, such as writable by its group or by others, so an account could give itself root. Make both 0644 root:root.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0003","technique":"T1078.003"}]},
{"id":"harden.files.crontab","version":1,"title":"System cron files can be changed by other users","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"(facts['file.etc_crontab.mode'] != '' && facts['file.etc_crontab.mode'] != '0644' && facts['file.etc_crontab.mode'] != '0640' && facts['file.etc_crontab.mode'] != '0600' && facts['file.etc_crontab.mode'] != '0444' && facts['file.etc_crontab.mode'] != '0440' && facts['file.etc_crontab.mode'] != '0400') || (facts['file.etc_cron_d.mode'] != '' && facts['file.etc_cron_d.mode'] != '0755' && facts['file.etc_cron_d.mode'] != '0750' && facts['file.etc_cron_d.mode'] != '0700' && facts['file.etc_cron_d.mode'] != '0555' && facts['file.etc_cron_d.mode'] != '0550' && facts['file.etc_cron_d.mode'] != '0500')","finding_message":"/etc/crontab or /etc/cron.d has a mode that lets more than root change it (accepted: 0644 or stricter for the file, 0755 or stricter for the directory), so others could schedule commands as root. Make them writable by root only.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0003","technique":"T1053.003"}]},
{"id":"harden.files.grub_cfg","version":1,"title":"The boot loader configuration is readable by all users","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"(facts['file.boot_grub2_grub_cfg.mode'] != '' && (facts['file.boot_grub2_grub_cfg.mode'].endsWith('4') || facts['file.boot_grub2_grub_cfg.mode'].endsWith('5') || facts['file.boot_grub2_grub_cfg.mode'].endsWith('6') || facts['file.boot_grub2_grub_cfg.mode'].endsWith('7'))) || (facts['file.boot_grub_grub_cfg.mode'] != '' && (facts['file.boot_grub_grub_cfg.mode'].endsWith('4') || facts['file.boot_grub_grub_cfg.mode'].endsWith('5') || facts['file.boot_grub_grub_cfg.mode'].endsWith('6') || facts['file.boot_grub_grub_cfg.mode'].endsWith('7')))","finding_message":"grub.cfg can be read by every user; it can hold the boot loader password hash and kernel options. Make it 0600 (or 0400) root:root.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1003"}]},
{"id":"harden.accounts.extra_uid0","version":1,"title":"An account other than root has uid 0","severity":"critical","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['accounts.uid0.count'] > 1 || (facts['accounts.uid0.count'] == 1 && !('root' in facts['accounts.uid0']))","finding_message":"An account other than root has uid 0, so it has every power root has. Remove it or give it its own uid.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0004","technique":"T1078.003"}]},
{"id":"harden.accounts.empty_password","version":1,"title":"An account has an empty password","severity":"critical","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['accounts.empty_password.count'] > 0","finding_message":"An account has an empty password field in /etc/shadow; depending on PAM it can log in without a password. Lock it (passwd -l) or set a password.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0001","technique":"T1078.003"}]},
{"id":"harden.accounts.system_shell","version":1,"title":"A system account has a login shell","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['accounts.shell_users.count'] > 0","finding_message":"A system account (uid 1 to 999) has a login shell, so it can be used to log in interactively. Set its shell to /usr/sbin/nologin unless it needs one.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0003","technique":"T1078.003"}]},
{"id":"harden.login.hash_method","version":1,"title":"Passwords are hashed with a weak method","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"facts['login_defs.encrypt_method'] != '' && !(facts['login_defs.encrypt_method'] == 'sha512' || facts['login_defs.encrypt_method'] == 'Sha512' || facts['login_defs.encrypt_method'] == 'SHA512' || facts['login_defs.encrypt_method'] == 'yescrypt' || facts['login_defs.encrypt_method'] == 'Yescrypt' || facts['login_defs.encrypt_method'] == 'YESCRYPT')","finding_message":"/etc/login.defs sets ENCRYPT_METHOD to something other than SHA512 or YESCRYPT, so new password hashes are easier to crack. Set ENCRYPT_METHOD SHA512 or YESCRYPT.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1110"}]},
{"id":"harden.login.pwquality_minlen","version":1,"title":"Passwords may be shorter than 12 characters","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"'pam_pwquality.so' in facts['pam.modules'] && facts['pam.pwquality.minlen'] < 12","finding_message":"pam_pwquality checks passwords but allows fewer than 12 characters (minlen, default 8). Set minlen = 12 or more in /etc/security/pwquality.conf.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1110"}]},
{"id":"harden.login.faillock","version":1,"title":"Failed logins never lock an account","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"!('pam_faillock.so' in facts['pam.modules']) || facts['pam.faillock.deny'] == 0","finding_message":"No PAM stack uses pam_faillock (or deny is 0), so passwords can be guessed without limit. Enable pam_faillock with deny = 5 or fewer.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0006","technique":"T1110"}]},
{"id":"harden.services.avahi","version":1,"title":"Avahi (mDNS) is enabled","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"'avahi-daemon.service' in facts['service.enabled'] || 'avahi-daemon.socket' in facts['service.enabled']","finding_message":"avahi-daemon is enabled: it announces the host and its services on the local network. Disable it on servers (systemctl disable --now avahi-daemon.service avahi-daemon.socket).","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0007","technique":"T1046"}]},
{"id":"harden.modules.rare_protocols","version":1,"title":"A rarely used network protocol module is loaded","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"'dccp' in facts['kernel.modules.loaded'] || 'sctp' in facts['kernel.modules.loaded'] || 'rds' in facts['kernel.modules.loaded'] || 'tipc' in facts['kernel.modules.loaded']","finding_message":"A rarely used network protocol (dccp, sctp, rds or tipc) is loaded; these have had remotely reachable kernel bugs. Unload it and block it in /etc/modprobe.d unless it is needed.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0008","technique":"T1210"}]},
{"id":"harden.lsm.selinux_off","version":1,"title":"SELinux is disabled","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"('fedora' in facts['os.id_like'] || 'rhel' in facts['os.id_like']) && facts['lsm.selinux'] == 'disabled'","finding_message":"SELinux is disabled on a Fedora/RHEL-family host, which removes its confinement of services. Enable it (SELINUX=enforcing) and relabel.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0112","technique":"T1685"}]},
{"id":"harden.lsm.selinux_permissive","version":1,"title":"SELinux only logs","severity":"low","confidence":90,"expression":"('fedora' in facts['os.id_like'] || 'rhel' in facts['os.id_like']) && facts['lsm.selinux'] == 'permissive'","finding_message":"SELinux is permissive on a Fedora/RHEL-family host: it logs denials but blocks nothing. Set it to enforcing.","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0112","technique":"T1685"}]},
{"id":"harden.lsm.apparmor_off","version":1,"title":"AppArmor is disabled","severity":"medium","confidence":90,"expression":"('debian' in facts['os.id_like'] || 'ubuntu' in facts['os.id_like']) && facts['lsm.apparmor'] == 'disabled'","finding_message":"AppArmor is disabled on a Debian/Ubuntu host, which removes its confinement of services. Enable it (apparmor=1 on the kernel command line, and the service).","attack":[{"tactic":"TA0112","technique":"T1685"}]}
]}
